title: Solubility
subtitle: Solubility of Solids and Gases in Liquids

intro.heading: Introduction
intro.content: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can be dissolved in a specified amount of solvent at a specific temperature. When no more solute can be dissolved in a solution, it is called a saturated solution.

henry.heading: Henry's Law
henry.content: At a constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of the liquid or solution.
